cwg.evidence_note: Endorses MPCA transfer value (360,000 SDG, about $150, 3 months) and guides JMMI. ai_summary.headline: MPC is 4% of a $2.9bn plan but about 81% funded; the wider cash story sits with the consortium.
ai_summary.narrative: The 2026 HNRP seeks $2.9bn for 20.4 million of 33.7 million people in need [s1][s2]. MPC is $121.3M, about 4% of requirements, targeting 1.0M households at 360,000 SDG (about $150) a month for three months [s3]. Live FTS data (5 November) show MPC far better funded than the plan overall: about 81% against 46.9% [s16], though the pooled-fund attribution view gives a higher figure. Outside the HNRP, CCS (now Collective Sudan) delivers MPCA through 18-19 partners and handles FSP procurement and a common payment architecture [s6][s10][s11]. Coverage remains thin: in over 50 of 57 mapped localities MPCA is under 10% of food assistance, and about 95% of the affected population reportedly receives nothing [s14]. The CWG's June 2026 position paper argues for sustaining MPCA as funding tightens [s5]. The JMMI is monthly and shows the SDG depreciating 34% in two months [s8]. Inference: much of the cash volume sits in consortium and SHF channels that the HNRP figures understate.
barriers: Bureaucratic and regulatory barriers delay cash programming [s5]
Currency depreciation (+34% in Feb-Apr 2026) erodes transfer value [s8]
Market and FSP data not linked to planning tools [s6]
No current feasibility assessment; the last is from 2021 [s7]
opportunities: Collective Sudan's shared FSP procurement and common payment system could serve as a platform for other actors [s10][s11]
Monthly JMMI and CWG-endorsed MPCA transfer value give an evidence base for advocacy [s3][s8]
data_gaps: modality preference: only a 'most dignified' figure (>90%), no forced-choice split

total_funding_usd.note: All incoming funding to the plan, pledges excluded. Matches the FTS plan summary.

mpc_usd.note: FTS single-cluster view of the Multi-Purpose Cash cluster; shared-cluster view US$100.1M. Incoming flows, pledges excluded.

ctp_usd.note: All flows tagged 'Cash transfer programming (CTP)', inside or outside the MPC cluster.

sectoral_cva_usd.note: Flows whose FTS modality field is 'Cash transfer programming (CTP)' and whose destination cluster is not multi-purpose cash: 46 flows. The CTP tag is set by the reporting donor or agency and is not applied consistently, so this is a floor, not a measure of sectoral cash. Largest: Food Security and Livelihoods US$5.5M, Protection US$5.1M, Water, Sanitation and Hygiene US$1.1M.

cva_usd.note: Union of the MPC cluster and the CTP tag. Widest defensible FTS cash figure; still a floor because untagged sectoral cash is invisible.

sectoral_cva_pct_of_total.note: sectoral_cva_usd as a share of total plan funding.

mpc_pct_of_total.note: MPC cluster funding as a share of total plan funding (single-cluster view).

fts_cva.caveat: FTS records funding, not transfers to people, and only to first-level recipients. Sectoral cash depends on a modality tag that reporters apply unevenly.

FTS does not see sub-grants, so this understates money that reaches local actors through international intermediaries.

localisation.caveat: FTS sees first-level recipients only; indicator 4.2 as defined (direct donor allocation to local partners) is therefore a floor. Chair roles come from public CWG pages and may be out of date.
